classification.difficultyReason: Read a boxplot and use quartile proportions to estimate counts in a survey of 200 people.

content.prompt: In a market survey, 200 people were asked how many hours of television they watched in the previous week. The results are presented in the boxplot below.

spec.description: Horizontal unfilled boxplot beneath a scale labelled from 0 to 20 in steps of 2. Whiskers have no end caps. Decorative source blue is replaced with house black.
spec.mathematics: Minimum 3, lower quartile 8, median 11, upper quartile 12, maximum 19; values are hours.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied boxplot remains visible in the question edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the maximum number of hours anyone watched television?

answer.worked: The right whisker ends at 19, so the maximum is 19 hours.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many people watched more than 8 hours of television?

answer.worked:
The lower quartile is 8 hours, so approximately 75% watched more than 8 hours.
$$\text{Number of people}=\frac{75}{100}\times200=150.$$
Approximately 150 people.

children.label: d
children.prompt: How many people watched between 8 hours and 11 hours of television?

answer.worked:
The interval from the lower quartile, 8 hours, to the median, 11 hours, contains approximately 25% of the data.
$$\text{Number of people}=\frac{25}{100}\times200=50.$$
Approximately 50 people.
